facts_of_case: Appellant-husband sought dissolution of marriage on grounds of cruelty and desertion. Respondent-wife claimed that parties belong to Tribal Community (Lambadies) and Family Court has no jurisdiction under Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: Sub-section 2 of Section 2 of Hindu Succession Act excludes members of any Scheduled Tribe from the application of the said Act only if they are not 'Hinduised' and do not follow Hindu traditions.
legal_principles.held: Sub-section 2 only excludes members of any Scheduled Tribe admittedly as per finding recorded in the present case though the parties originally belong to the Santhal Scheduled Tribe they are Hinduised and they are following the Hindu traditions.
cited_cases: Labishwar Manjhi vs. Pran Manjhi And Ors (2000) 8 SCC 587
use_in: divorce cases involving Hindu Succession Act
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in determining the applicability of Hindu Succession Act to Scheduled Tribes

legal_principles.principle: Custom may be proved for the determination of civil rights of parties, including their status, and may be used for the purposes of proving the ingredients of an offence.
legal_principles.held: No custom can create an offence as it essentially deals with the civil rights of the parties and no person can be convicted of any offence except for violation of law in force at the time of commission of the act charged.
cited_cases: Dr. Surajmani Stella Kujur vs. Durga Charan Hansdah
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — significance in understanding the role of custom in determining civil rights

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed, and the impugned order dated 28.09.2012 is set aside.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
advising on maintenance and alimony in a family court appeal
assisting with property division in a joint family dispute
